reasons: The lake record identifies Brewer v. Williams/Brewer, Warden v. Williams as a verified U.S. Supreme Court case, docket 74-1263, year 1977.
The official citation in the lake record is 430 U.S. 387, with parallels 97 S. Ct. 1232 and 51 L. Ed. 2d 424; the content page uses 430 U.S. 387 (1977) and U.S. Supreme Court.
residual_risks: The cached opinion header says Decided March 23, 1977, while the page/lake date_decided fields say 1977-05-16; no separate date_decided assertion row was supplied.

defect.evidence_quote: Whatever else it may mean, the right to counsel granted by the Sixth and Fourteenth Amendments means at least that a person is entitled to the help of a lawyer at or after the time that judicial proceedings have been initiated against him"whether by way of formal charge, preliminary hearing, indictment, information, or arraignment."
defect.locator_note: text/Brewer v. Williams__aa921b.txt line 45 contains the actual passage; lake pinpoints[].quote for pin-398 contains content-page prose and Markdown headings instead.
defect.problem: pin-398's lake/payload quote is not the quoted rule passage from the opinion. It is a harvested slice of the content page/background/headings, ending before the actual rule quote. The displayed rule quote is substantively supported, but the pinpoint quote record is not character-faithful to the opinion text.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace pin-398's quote with the actual page-398 passage beginning with the Sixth/Fourteenth Amendment right-to-counsel language, and anchor it to page 398. If exact fidelity is required, preserve the source punctuation/encoding rather than the page's normalized punctuation.

reasons: The payload quote begins with 'suggesting the child deserved a Christian burial...' and includes '## Issue'/'## Rule' text, which is not an opinion quote.
The opinion text contains the actual right-attachment language at the 398 star page.
The content page's visible quote also normalizes punctuation around the embedded quotation, so it is not strictly character-faithful to the cached text.
residual_risks: The text cache appears to preserve a mojibake dash character, so the corpus should define whether exact_quote is byte/character exact or normalized.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Store a clean exact quote for pin-398 separately from any normalized display quote.

defect.evidence_quote: There can be no serious doubt, either, that Detective Leaming deliberately and designedly set out to elicit information from Williams just as surely asand perhaps more effectively thanif he had formally interrogated him.
defect.locator_note: text/Brewer v. Williams__aa921b.txt line 47; the preceding star pagination places the passage on 430 U.S. 399.
defect.problem: The quote's words and page support are correct, but the punctuation is not character-faithful: the cached opinion has no-space dash characters around 'and perhaps more effectively than,' while the page/lake quote uses spaced em dashes.
defect.proposed_fix: Use the cached-text punctuation exactly, or mark the displayed quote as normalized rather than exact.

reasons: The same sentence appears in the opinion text at the claimed location.
The only fidelity defect found is punctuation/spacing around the dash characters.
The proposition of deliberate elicitation is supported by the quoted passage and surrounding text.
residual_risks: Same normalization issue as pin-398: exact and display quotes should not be conflated.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Maintain exact_quote and normalized_display_quote fields for dash and quotation-mark normalization.

reasons: Treatment/currency is outside Lens A, so no Lens A treatment finding is raised.
The disclosed lake/content treatment fields state field_i_validity=good_law, varies_by_point=false, and a scope note limiting Nix v. Williams to the exclusionary-remedy issue.
residual_risks: No Lens B treatment audit was performed.
